## claude.ai Crypto.com
Crypto.com Exchange MCP Server - Real-time cryptocurrency market data and interactive widgets.

Available Tools:
- get_widget: Get any interactive widget by name (orderbook, trades, candles)
- get_market_orderbook: Order book snapshot (bids/asks)
- get_market_trades: Recent trade history
- get_market_candles: OHLCV candle data for charting

All tools return structured responses with success/error status and metadata.
Widget can be embedded in ChatGPT or any HTML context.

Example usage:
1. Get widget: get_widget(widget_name='orderbook')
2. Get BTC order book: get_market_orderbook(symbol='BTC_USDT', depth=20)
3. Get ETH trades: get_market_trades(symbol='ETH_USDT', limit=50)
4. Get BTC 4h candles: get_market_candles(symbol='BTC_USDT', interval='4h', limit=100)

- _OUTLOOK: Draft a fully-formatted email into Outlook for Mac — opens a ready-to-review compose window, never sends. Drives classic Outlook via AppleScript with HTML content so paragraphs, bullet lists, and numbered lists render correctly; degrades to a plain-text mailto draft if only New Outlook is present. Pulls recipient addresses from CONTACTS.md and writes in Nick's email voice. USE WHEN draft an email, write an email to X, email X about Y, open a draft in Outlook, compose an email, reply to X, send an email (draft it for review). NOT FOR actually transmitting mail unattended (this is draft-only), Gmail/web mail (no Outlook desktop), or bulk/broadcast sends (use _BROADCAST). Mac only — requires osascript.
- Agents: Compose CUSTOM agents from Base Traits + Voice + Specialization, and manage predefined functional TEAMS. Traits combine expertise (security, technical, research), personality (skeptical, analytical, enthusiastic), and approach (thorough, rapid, systematic). ComposeAgent.ts merges base + user config, outputs unique prompt + ElevenLabs voice + prosody. Predefined teams: engineering, architecture, marketing, design, security, research, content, strategy — each YAML-configured with roles, tensions, and specialist members. Observer team variant: read-only oversight agents that vote continue/halt/escalate against the tool-activity audit log (high-blast-radius or unattended runs only). USE WHEN create custom agents, spin up agents, specialized agents, agent personalities, available traits, list traits, agent voices, compose agent, spawn parallel agents, launch agents, engineering team, architecture team, marketing team, design team, security team, research team, content team, strategy team, get the team on this, observer team, audit agents. NOT FOR ad-hoc swarms or TeamCreate coordination (use Delegation). NOT FOR single-threaded delegation without unique identities (use Delegation Task).
- ApertureOscillation: 3-pass scope oscillation that holds a question constant while shifting the scope envelope — narrow/tactical, wide/strategic, then synthesis — to surface design tensions invisible at any single zoom level. Requires two distinct inputs: the tactical target (what you're building) and strategic context (the larger system it serves). Pass 1 captures the component's own internal logic. Pass 2 reveals what the system needs it to be. Pass 3 finds where those views diverge — that delta is the output. Produces: design tensions, scope recommendations, and coherence assessments. Single workflow: Workflows/Oscillate.md. BPE-fragile — quarterly test recommended to verify smarter models don't naturally oscillate scope without prompting. Best integration point: Algorithm OBSERVE phase (before ISC) or THINK phase (before approach commitment). NOT a lens rotation (that's IterativeDepth) and NOT idea generation (that's BeCreative). NOT FOR deep incident causal chains (use RootCauseAnalysis) or assumption decomposition (use FirstPrinciples). USE WHEN aperture oscillation, oscillate scope, zoom in and out, tactical vs strategic, scope framing, design tension, architecture decision, feature fits system, system coherence check, local vs global design, build this inside that, wrong scope, design review, scope negotiation.
- Aphorisms: Manages a curated aphorism collection with full CRUD — content-based matching, themed search, thinker research, and database maintenance. Organizes quotes by author, theme, context, and newsletter usage history to prevent repetition. Four workflows: FindAphorism (analyze newsletter content, match themes, return 3-5 ranked recommendations with rationale), AddAphorism (parse quote + author, extract themes, validate uniqueness, update theme index), ResearchThinker (deep research on philosopher, add sourced quotes to database), SearchAphorisms (search by theme, keyword, or author). Database at ~/.claude/skills/aphorisms/Database/aphorisms.md — stores full quote text, author attribution, theme tags, context/background, source reference, and usage history per entry. Theme index supports 12+ categories: Work Ethic, Resilience, Learning, Stoicism, Risk, Wisdom, Truth-seeking, Excellence, Curiosity, Freedom, Rationality, Clarity. Supported thinkers: Hitchens, Feynman, Deutsch, Sam Harris, Spinoza, plus any requested author. Newsletter integration: tracks which quotes used in which issues to enforce variety; content theme extraction drives automated matching. USE WHEN: aphorism, quote, saying, find a quote, research thinker, add aphorism, search aphorisms, quote for newsletter, what did X say about, quotes about [topic], quote bank, find matching quote, quote collection, add this quote, check usage history. NOT FOR general creative writing or social media post generation — those go through dedicated writing/social skill…
- Apify: Scrape social media platforms, business data, and e-commerce via Apify actors — Instagram profiles/posts/hashtags/comments, LinkedIn profiles/jobs/posts, TikTok profiles/hashtags/videos/comments, YouTube channels/search/comments, Facebook posts/groups/comments, Google Maps business search with contact/review/image extraction, Amazon products/reviews/pricing, and general-purpose multi-page web crawling with custom pageFunction extraction logic. File-based TypeScript wrappers (scrapeInstagramProfile, searchGoogleMaps, scrapeAmazonProduct, scrapeWebsite, etc.) filter and transform data in code before returning to model context, achieving 95-99% token savings over direct MCP protocol. Parallel multi-platform queries via Promise.all for social listening dashboards. Lead enrichment pipeline: Google Maps → qualified filter → optional LinkedIn enrichment. Competitive analysis across Instagram, YouTube, and TikTok simultaneously. USE WHEN scrape Instagram, scrape LinkedIn, scrape TikTok, scrape YouTube, scrape Facebook, Google Maps leads, Amazon reviews, business intelligence, multi-platform social listening, competitive analysis, lead generation, social monitoring, Apify actors, web crawl, extract contacts. NOT FOR X/Twitter bookmarks (use a dedicated X-API skill) or progressive scraping (use BrightData).
- Art: Generates static visual content across 20+ formats via Flux, Nano Banana Pro (Gemini 3 Pro), and GPT-Image-1. Covers blog header illustrations, editorial art, Mermaid flowcharts, technical architecture diagrams, D3.js dashboards, taxonomies, timelines, 2x2 framework matrices, comparisons, annotated screenshots, recipe cards, aphorism/quote cards, conceptual maps, stat cards, comic panels, YouTube thumbnails, PAI pack icons, and brand-logo wallpapers. Named workflows: Essay, D3Dashboards, Visualize, Mermaid, TechnicalDiagrams, Taxonomies, Timelines, Frameworks, Comparisons, AnnotatedScreenshots, RecipeCards, Aphorisms, Maps, Stats, Comics, YouTubeThumbnailChecklist, AdHocYouTubeThumbnail, CreatePAIPackIcon, LogoWallpaper, RemoveBackground. SKILLCUSTOMIZATIONS loads PREFERENCES.md, CharacterSpecs.md, and SceneConstruction.md. --remove-bg flag produces transparent-background PNG (can produce black backgrounds — verify visually). Up to 14 reference images per request (5 human, 6 object Gemini API limit). Output staged to ~/Downloads/ for preview before any project directory copy. Nano Banana Pro uses --size for resolution tier 1K/2K/4K and separate --aspect-ratio. USE WHEN: art, illustration, diagram, flowchart, infographic, header image, thumbnail, visualize, generate image, mermaid, architecture diagram, comic, icon, blog art, framework diagram, D3 chart, remove background, wallpaper. NOT FOR video or animation (use Remotion). NOT FOR the user's personal portrait/headshot (use a dedicated headshot skill).
- ArXiv: Search and retrieve arXiv academic papers by topic, category, or paper ID — with AlphaXiv-enriched AI-generated overviews. Uses arXiv Atom API (no auth) for discovery and search across cs.AI, cs.LG, cs.CL (NLP/LLMs), cs.CR (security), cs.MA (multi-agent), cs.SE, and cs.IR. Supports title (ti:), abstract (abs:), author (au:), and category (cat:) search fields with boolean operators (AND, OR, ANDNOT); sorts by lastUpdatedDate or relevance; paginates up to 2,000 results per call with 3s rate limit between calls. AlphaXiv enrichment fetches markdown summaries from alphaxiv.org/overview/{ID}.md; full text from alphaxiv.org/abs/{ID}.md as fallback; 404 means summary not yet generated. Workflows: Latest (new papers by category), Search (topic/keyword search), Paper (single paper deep-dive by ID or URL). API returns Atom XML — parse with text processing, not jq. HTTPS required with -L flag; check published date not lastUpdatedDate for truly new submissions. Output: paper title, authors, abstract, AlphaXiv summary, and direct arXiv URL. USE WHEN arxiv, papers, latest papers, research papers, new papers, what's new in AI research, recent ML papers, paper lookup, arxiv search, find paper by ID, summarize paper, latest NLP research, latest LLM papers, multi-agent papers, cs.AI latest, AI safety papers, software engineering papers, information retrieval papers. NOT FOR general web research (use Research), extracting content from arbitrary URLs (use Parser), or cybersecurity annual report analysis (use AnnualReports).
- AudioEditor: AI-powered audio and video editing pipeline: Whisper word-level transcription (insanely-fast-whisper on MPS) → Claude segment classification (KEEP / CUT_FILLER / CUT_FALSE_START / CUT_STUTTER / CUT_DEAD_AIR / CUT_EDIT_MARKER) → ffmpeg execution with 40ms qsin crossfades and room-tone gap fill → optional Cleanvoice API cloud polish for mouth sounds and loudness normalization. Distinguishes rhetorical pauses from accidental ones. Breaths attenuated to 50% volume (not removed). Preview mode (--preview flag) shows proposed cuts without modifying audio. Aggressive mode (--aggressive flag) applies tighter filler detection thresholds. Polish step (--polish flag) uploads to Cleanvoice API for mouth sound removal and loudness normalization — confirm before cloud upload of sensitive content. Pipeline tools: Transcribe.ts, Analyze.ts, Edit.ts, Polish.ts, Pipeline.ts. Single workflow: Clean.md. Requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; CLEANVOICE_API_KEY optional for polish step. USE WHEN: clean audio, edit audio, remove filler words, clean podcast, remove ums, cut dead air, polish audio, trim recording, audio cleanup, cut stutters, edit interview recording, preview edits, aggressive clean. NOT FOR video composition or animation (use Remotion).
- BeCreative: Divergent ideation and corpus expansion using Verbalized Sampling + extended thinking. Single-shot mode generates 5 internally diverse candidates (p<0.10 each) and surfaces the strongest. Multi-turn mode expands a small seed corpus (5-20 examples) into a diverse N-example dataset for evals, training, or test sets. Research-backed: Zhang et al. 2025 (arXiv:2510.01171) — 1.6-2.1x diversity increase on creative writing, 25.7% quality improvement, and synthetic-data downstream accuracy lift 30.6% → 37.5% on math benchmarks. Seven workflows: StandardCreativity, MaximumCreativity, IdeaGeneration, TreeOfThoughts, DomainSpecific, TechnicalCreativityGemini3 for algorithmic/architecture work, and SyntheticDataExpansion for VS-Multi corpus growth. lastPrompt: What does it involve to get allow my app to be able to access Aus Bank feeds.

content.text:
Recommendation up front: don't try to access bank feeds directly. For any app you're building, integrate a CDR-accredited aggregator (Basiq is the default choice in Australia). Direct access means becoming a regulated data recipient, which is months of work and ongoing compliance cost you almost certainly don't want to carry.

Here's the full landscape so the trade-off is clear.

## The two regimes you're choosing between

**1. CDR / Open Banking (the regulated, sanctioned path)**
This is the government Consumer Data Right framework. Banks must expose customer transaction data via standardised APIs, but only to accredited recipients, and only with explicit consumer consent. To touch that data you need an accreditation status with the ACCC. The tiers, heaviest to lightest:

- **Unrestricted ADR (Accredited Data Recipient)** — full accreditation. Requires an independent information security assurance assessment (ASAE 3150), CDR policy, attestations, insurance, ongoing reporting. Realistically 3-6+ months and tens of thousands of dollars. This is what aggregators themselves hold.
- **Sponsored / Affiliate** — a principal ADR sponsors you; lighter security bar but you still carry obligations.
- **CDR Representative** — you operate under a principal's accreditation via a contract. Fastest regulated route; the principal is liable and does the heavy lifting. Common for fintechs.
- **Trusted Adviser / CDR Insights** — narrow tiers for accountants, advisers, or insight-only (not raw transactions).

**2. Screen scraping (legacy, being phased out)**
User hands over their banking login, a service logs in as them and scrapes transactions. Yodlee and Basiq's legacy mode do this. It's being actively deprecated, several banks block it, and it breaches most banks' T&Cs. Don't build new on it.

## The practical path: use an aggregator

A CDR-accredited platform sits between you and the banks. You integrate one API, they hold the accreditation, run the consent UI, and normalise data across institutions. Main players in AU:

- **Basiq** — Australian, dominant, best developer experience. CDR + sandbox + consent flows. Default pick.
- **Frollo** — Australian ADR, white-label and SDK-heavy, good if you want a packaged money-management UX.
- **Adatree / Biza.io** — CDR-infrastructure-as-a-service if you eventually want your own accreditation but want them to operate it.
- **Envestnet Yodlee, Mastercard Open Banking** — global players with AU coverage; heavier, more enterprise.

What integrating one actually involves: sign up and get sandbox keys, build the consent flow (redirect the user to authorise their bank, get a token), call the accounts/transactions endpoints, handle consent expiry/refresh (CDR consents are time-boxed, typically up to 12 months, then re-consent), and store data in line with their and CDR data-handling rules. You can be pulling real transactions in days, not months.

## One thing worth flagging for your stack

If "my app" is **envelope-os**, you already have bank feeds — PocketSmith aggregates them for you (it uses Yodlee/Basiq under the hood), and you're consuming them through the PocketSmith API. You don't need your own feed access at all unless you're moving off PocketSmith. If this is a *new* product (or you want feeds independent of PocketSmith), the Basiq route above is the move.

needs input: which app is this for — envelope-os (you already have feeds via PocketSmith), or a new product? And do you want raw transaction feeds or just balances/insights? Tell me and I'll spec the Basiq integration (or the PocketSmith path) concretely.

1	## The Algorithm 6.3.0
2	
3	> Change history, migration recipes, and rollback steps live in `changelog.md` (read on demand). This file is doctrine only — what the Algorithm does this run.
4	
5	### Doctrine — Read This First, Internalize It
6	
7	**Every Algorithm run does one thing: transition from CURRENT STATE to IDEAL STATE.** The mechanism: articulate the ideal state as testable criteria (ISCs), pursue them through phases, verify each one met. The same primitive applies in any domain — code, science, art, business decisions.
8	
9	**The ISA is one primitive with five identities.** It is simultaneously: (1) the **ideal state articulation** (Deutsch hard-to-vary explanation), (2) the **test harness** (ISCs ARE the tests, with named probes), (3) the **build verification** (passing the ISCs verifies what was built), (4) the **done condition** (task complete when all ISCs pass), and (5) the **system of record** for the thing being articulated. Don't invent parallel artifacts (acceptance.yaml, acceptance.ts, separate test specs) — the ISA already covers this surface. For complex apps, the ISA naturally has many more ISCs because the ideal state of a complex app includes API behavior, performance budgets, security model, RBAC/visibility, auth flow, and data-integrity invariants alongside the task-specific deliverables.
10	
11	**The unit is the thing being articulated, not the task.** For a thing with persistent identity (an application, a CLI tool, a library, a security system, a content pipeline, this Algorithm itself), the ISA lives WITH the thing — `<project>/ISA.md` in its repo — and is the system of record for it. Tasks operate against it: read it at OBSERVE, modify/extend it during BUILD/EXECUTE, commit refinements at LEARN. Iteration on the project IS iteration on the ISA. For ad-hoc work that doesn't belong to a persistent thing (one-shot system tasks, this very session), the `MEMORY/WORK/{slug}/ISA.md` pattern stays — that's the ISA of a one-shot effort.
12	
13	**The ISA has twelve sections (NEW v6.2.0).** Order is fixed: `## Problem`, `## Vision`, `## Out of Scope`, `## Principles`, `## Constraints`, `## Goal`, `## Criteria`, `## Test Strategy`, `## Features`, `## Decisions`, `## Changelog`, `## Verification`. Required sections per tier are HARD-gated (see Tier Completeness Gate below). Empty sections never appear — Bitter Pill discipline preserved. Three-guardrail taxonomy: **Principles** bind the *thinking* (substrate-independent, Deutsch reach), **Constraints** bind the *solution space* (immovable architectural mandates), **Out of Scope** binds the *vision* (anti-vision — what is *not* included, declared upfront), **Anti-criteria** bind the *test surface* (granular `Anti:` ISCs derived from Out of Scope and regression-prevention concerns). The first three are author-stated; anti-criteria are derived probes.
14	
15	**The ISA Skill (NEW v6.2.0)** at `~/.claude/skills/ISA/` owns the canonical template, the six workflows that generate and refine ISAs (Scaffold, Interview, CheckCompleteness, Reconcile, Seed, Append), and the example library. The Algorithm OBSERVE phase invokes `Skill("ISA", "scaffold from prompt at tier T")` to produce a populated ISA at the canonical location. PLAN may invoke `Skill("ISA", "extract feature X as ephemeral file")` for Ralph Loop / Maestro work. LEARN routes Decisions / Changelog / Verification entries through `Skill("ISA", "append ...")` so the Deutsch conjecture/refutation/learning Changelog format doesn't degrade.
16	
17	**The ISA is a living articulation.** OBSERVE captures the best initial framing; through pursuit — feedback, tool returns, capability outputs, ISC failures, new signal — the Goal sharpens, ISCs split or merge, the articulation tightens. Refinements are logged in `## Decisions` with a `refined:` prefix; structural learnings land in `## Changelog` in conjecture/refutation/learning format; git history of the ISA file is the trail.
18	
19	**ID-stability rule (NEW v6.2.0):** ISC IDs never re-number on edit. Splits become `ISC-N.M` (parent preserved); drops become tombstones (`- [ ] ISC-N: [DROPPED — see Decisions]`). Reconcile depends on this; renumbering breaks ephemeral feature reconciliation silently.

21	**The experiential metric is euphoric surprise** — what the user feels when work converges on what they actually wanted: an answer that clicks in a way they couldn't have predicted but instantly recognize as true. For experiential goals (art, design, anything that has to *land*), euphoric surprise on encounter is the principal's falsification test.
22	
23	**Core loop:** current state → ideal state, with the ISA as the living articulation of done, ISCs as the testable claims that decompose it, verification as the proof that each claim was met, refinement as the writing tightening through pursuit. **Goal: euphoric surprise on convergence.**

71	### Mode Classification (v6.3.0)
72	
73	**Mode and tier are decided by a Sonnet classifier at UserPromptSubmit, not by the executor.** `hooks/PromptProcessing.hook.ts` runs on every top-level prompt, calls Sonnet via the same subscription-billed `claude` subprocess pattern Inference.ts uses, and writes a single line into additionalContext:
74	
75	```
76	MODE: MINIMAL | NATIVE | ALGORITHM   (always present)
77	TIER: E1 | E2 | E3 | E4 | E5         (present iff MODE=ALGORITHM)
78	REASON: <one sentence>
79	SOURCE: classifier | fail-safe
80	```
81	
82	The executor reads this directly. **No regex fallback. No model judgment.** If `MODE` is MINIMAL or NATIVE, the executor uses the corresponding format from CLAUDE.md and stops. If `MODE` is ALGORITHM, the executor enters the Algorithm at the named `TIER`.
83	
84	**Classifier rules (encoded in the hook's system prompt):**
85	
86	- **MINIMAL** — greetings, ratings, single-token acknowledgments.
87	- **NATIVE** — single fact lookup OR single-line edit on a named file OR one command run, AND no new artifact created, AND no multi-step plan.
88	- **ALGORITHM** — everything else. Includes any build/create/make/implement/design/refactor/migrate/integrate request, anything touching multiple files, anything ambiguous, anything affecting doctrine/system-prompt/hooks/CLAUDE.md/Algorithm/ISA, anything spanning multiple projects, any meta-question about the system itself.
89	- **Tier (ALGORITHM only)** — E1 trivial (~<90s), E2 single-domain (~3min), E3 multi-file substantial (~10min), E4 cross-cutting/doctrine/architecture (~30min), E5 comprehensive (>2h). Bias higher when in doubt.
90	
91	**Override hierarchy (executor side):**
92	
93	1. Explicit `/e1`–`/e5` in the prompt forces tier (and forces ALGORITHM mode if MINIMAL/NATIVE was returned).
94	2. Otherwise honor classifier output verbatim.
95	3. **Conversation-context override:** if the classifier returns MINIMAL/NATIVE on a prompt that the conversation context makes clearly ALGORITHM-shaped (e.g., "yes" answering a multi-step proposal, "do it" approving an architecture change), the executor escalates to the appropriate tier and notes the mismatch in `## Decisions`. The classifier sees the prompt in isolation; the executor sees the thread.
96	
97	**Fail-safe.** Any classifier error path — timeout (25s), non-zero exit, unparseable JSON — defaults to ALGORITHM E3 with `SOURCE: fail-safe` in REASON. Conservative-by-default: under-escalation is the failure mode this system was built to prevent.
98	
99	**Telemetry.** Every classification is logged to `MEMORY/OBSERVABILITY/mode-classifier.jsonl` with prompt excerpt, mode, tier, reason, source, and latency. Audit weekly: classifier-vs-fail-safe ratio, average latency, downstream override rate.
100	
101	**Coverage.** The classifier fires on `UserPromptSubmit` — top-level prompts only. Subagent prompts inherit whatever the primary picked. Sonnet latency adds ~3-8s per prompt; this is the deliberate cost of better judgment than regex could provide.

172	### ISC Quality System
173	
174	**Every criterion describes one verifiable end-state.** The operational test is granularity:
175	
176	> **Split until each criterion is one binary tool probe.** A criterion is granular enough when a single tool call (`Read`, `Grep`, `Bash`, `curl`, screenshot, `SELECT`, `bun test`, etc.) returns yes/no on whether it's met. If you cannot name the probe, the criterion is not yet atomic — split it. If the criterion needs human judgment, name the tool-verifiable proxy that stands in for the judgment.
177	
178	**Tier floor:** the granularity rule produces a natural N. At E2+, that N must meet the tier ISC floor (E2 ≥16, E3 ≥32, E4 ≥128, E5 ≥256). For complex-app project ISAs, the ISC count naturally runs much higher. E1 has no floor — fast-path stays fast.
179	
180	**Splitting Test** — apply to every criterion as you write it:
181	
182	| Test | Split when... |
183	|------|--------------|
184	| "And"/"With" | Joins two verifiable things |
185	| Independent failure | Part A can pass while B fails |
186	| Scope words | "all", "every", "complete" → enumerate |
187	| Domain boundary | Crosses UI/API/data/logic → one per boundary |
188	| **No nameable probe** | You can't say which tool would verify it |
189	
190	**Format:** `- [ ] ISC-N: criterion text` — the criterion phrasing reveals its category. **All ISCs number sequentially as `ISC-N`** — anti-criteria included. ID-stability rule applies: never re-number on edit; splits become `ISC-N.M`.
191	
192	**Two doctrinal ISC kinds preserved as prose prefix conventions:**
193	
194	| Kind | Surface form | Rule |
195	|------|--------------|------|
196	| **Anti-criterion** — must NOT happen | `- [ ] ISC-N: Anti: <what must NOT happen>` | **≥1 required** |
197	| **Antecedent** — precondition for target experience | `- [ ] ISC-N: Antecedent: <precondition>` | **≥1 required when goal is experiential** |
198	
199	**For complex-app projects: the ISA test surface includes (non-exhaustive):**
200	- **Functional** — features work end-to-end
201	- **API** — endpoints exist, return expected shape, handle errors
202	- **Auth** — sign-in/out, token expiry, magic-link flow, session lifecycle
203	- **Authorization (RBAC/visibility)** — role X can/cannot reach endpoint Y
204	- **Performance** — latency budgets per route, bundle sizes, query times
205	- **Security model** — input validation, output encoding, CSRF, rate limits, secret handling
206	- **Data integrity** — schema invariants, foreign-key consistency, idempotency
207	- **Build & deploy** — `bun build` succeeds, typecheck clean, deploy version matches
208	- **Operational** — `/health` returns 200, error budget within SLO, synthetic monitor up
209	
210	These aren't "in addition to" the ISA — they ARE the ISA. The ISA is the test harness because the ISCs are the tests.
211	
212	**Allowed status markers:**
213	- `- [ ]` — pending, not yet verified
214	- `- [x]` — passed, verified with evidence
215	- `- [DEFERRED-VERIFY]` — passed in code/intent but live probe is impossible at execution time. **Requires a follow-up task ID in the verification notes.** Cannot be marked `[x]` until the deferred probe runs.

## The Algorithm 6.3.0

> Change history, migration recipes, and rollback steps live in `changelog.md` (read on demand). This file is doctrine only — what the Algorithm does this run.

### Doctrine — Read This First, Internalize It

**Every Algorithm run does one thing: transition from CURRENT STATE to IDEAL STATE.** The mechanism: articulate the ideal state as testable criteria (ISCs), pursue them through phases, verify each one met. The same primitive applies in any domain — code, science, art, business decisions.

**The ISA is one primitive with five identities.** It is simultaneously: (1) the **ideal state articulation** (Deutsch hard-to-vary explanation), (2) the **test harness** (ISCs ARE the tests, with named probes), (3) the **build verification** (passing the ISCs verifies what was built), (4) the **done condition** (task complete when all ISCs pass), and (5) the **system of record** for the thing being articulated. Don't invent parallel artifacts (acceptance.yaml, acceptance.ts, separate test specs) — the ISA already covers this surface. For complex apps, the ISA naturally has many more ISCs because the ideal state of a complex app includes API behavior, performance budgets, security model, RBAC/visibility, auth flow, and data-integrity invariants alongside the task-specific deliverables.

**The unit is the thing being articulated, not the task.** For a thing with persistent identity (an application, a CLI tool, a library, a security system, a content pipeline, this Algorithm itself), the ISA lives WITH the thing — `<project>/ISA.md` in its repo — and is the system of record for it. Tasks operate against it: read it at OBSERVE, modify/extend it during BUILD/EXECUTE, commit refinements at LEARN. Iteration on the project IS iteration on the ISA. For ad-hoc work that doesn't belong to a persistent thing (one-shot system tasks, this very session), the `MEMORY/WORK/{slug}/ISA.md` pattern stays — that's the ISA of a one-shot effort.

**The ISA has twelve sections (NEW v6.2.0).** Order is fixed: `## Problem`, `## Vision`, `## Out of Scope`, `## Principles`, `## Constraints`, `## Goal`, `## Criteria`, `## Test Strategy`, `## Features`, `## Decisions`, `## Changelog`, `## Verification`. Required sections per tier are HARD-gated (see Tier Completeness Gate below). Empty sections never appear — Bitter Pill discipline preserved. Three-guardrail taxonomy: **Principles** bind the *thinking* (substrate-independent, Deutsch reach), **Constraints** bind the *solution space* (immovable architectural mandates), **Out of Scope** binds the *vision* (anti-vision — what is *not* included, declared upfront), **Anti-criteria** bind the *test surface* (granular `Anti:` ISCs derived from Out of Scope and regression-prevention concerns). The first three are author-stated; anti-criteria are derived probes.

**The ISA Skill (NEW v6.2.0)** at `~/.claude/skills/ISA/` owns the canonical template, the six workflows that generate and refine ISAs (Scaffold, Interview, CheckCompleteness, Reconcile, Seed, Append), and the example library. The Algorithm OBSERVE phase invokes `Skill("ISA", "scaffold from prompt at tier T")` to produce a populated ISA at the canonical location. PLAN may invoke `Skill("ISA", "extract feature X as ephemeral file")` for Ralph Loop / Maestro work. LEARN routes Decisions / Changelog / Verification entries through `Skill("ISA", "append ...")` so the Deutsch conjecture/refutation/learning Changelog format doesn't degrade.

**The ISA is a living articulation.** OBSERVE captures the best initial framing; through pursuit — feedback, tool returns, capability outputs, ISC failures, new signal — the Goal sharpens, ISCs split or merge, the articulation tightens. Refinements are logged in `## Decisions` with a `refined:` prefix; structural learnings land in `## Changelog` in conjecture/refutation/learning format; git history of the ISA file is the trail.

**ID-stability rule (NEW v6.2.0):** ISC IDs never re-number on edit. Splits become `ISC-N.M` (parent preserved); drops become tombstones (`- [ ] ISC-N: [DROPPED — see Decisions]`). Reconcile depends on this; renumbering breaks ephemeral feature reconciliation silently.

**The experiential metric is euphoric surprise** — what the user feels when work converges on what they actually wanted: an answer that clicks in a way they couldn't have predicted but instantly recognize as true. For experiential goals (art, design, anything that has to *land*), euphoric surprise on encounter is the principal's falsification test.

**Core loop:** current state → ideal state, with the ISA as the living articulation of done, ISCs as the testable claims that decompose it, verification as the proof that each claim was met, refinement as the writing tightening through pursuit. **Goal: euphoric surprise on convergence.**

### Effort Levels

| Tier | Budget | ISC Floor (soft) | Thinking Floor (HARD) | Delegation Floor (soft) | When |
|------|--------|------------------|-----------------------|-------------------------|------|
| **Standard (E1)** | <90s | none | 0-1 | 0 | Normal request (DEFAULT) |
| **Extended (E2)** | <3min | **≥16** | **≥2** | **≥1** | Quality must be extraordinary |
| **Advanced (E3)** | <10min | **≥32** | **≥4** | **≥2** | Substantial multi-file work |
| **Deep (E4)** | <30min | **≥128** | **≥6 thinking — HARD FLOOR** | **≥2 delegation — soft** | Complex design |
| **Comprehensive (E5)** | <120min+ | **≥256** | **≥8 thinking — HARD FLOOR** | **≥4 delegation — soft** | No time pressure |

**The time budget is the hard constraint set by tier.** ISC floor (E2+) is a soft minimum on the count axis. The capability floor splits into two axes:

**1. Thinking-capability floor (HARD, v6.1.0 — CLOSED ENUMERATION as of v6.3.0).** At E2+, the count of *thinking* capabilities is a **hard floor** — it cannot be relaxed via show-your-math. Difficult work earns thinking depth, full stop.

**The thinking-capability vocabulary is a CLOSED ENUMERATION.** Selection MUST come verbatim from this list — the same names that appear in `capabilities.md` § Thinking & Analysis Capabilities. Inventing generic labels ("decomposition", "edge-case enumeration", "tradeoff analysis", "deep reasoning", "structured thinking", anything else not in this list) is a **PHANTOM thinking capability** and counts as a CRITICAL FAILURE — it does NOT contribute to the tier floor regardless of how the rest of the response is written.

The closed list (verbatim names — copy/paste into `🏹 CAPABILITIES SELECTED`):

- **IterativeDepth** — multi-angle exploration; default at Extended+ when budget allows
- **ApertureOscillation** — tactical/strategic scope oscillation
- **FeedbackMemoryConsult** — grep prior `feedback_*.md` for matching mistakes
- **Advisor** — commitment-boundary second-opinion via `Inference.ts --mode advisor`
- **ReReadCheck** — final gate, re-read user's last message verbatim
- **FirstPrinciples** — physics-style deconstruct/challenge/rebuild
- **SystemsThinking** — Iceberg, causal loops, Meadows leverage points
- **RootCauseAnalysis** — 5 Whys, Fishbone, Apollo, Swiss Cheese
- **Council** — multi-agent debate with visible transcripts
- **RedTeam** — 32-agent adversarial stress-test
- **Science** — hypothesis-plural falsifiable experiments
- **BeCreative** — Verbalized Sampling divergent ideation
- **Ideate** — 9-phase evolutionary idea generation

E2 is structured-but-quick. E3 is substantial middle-tier work. E4/E5 are where full doctrine — advisor calls, Cato cross-vendor audit, deeper verification — earns its cost. Never let ceremony eat the budget; the only acceptable reason to spend a tier's time is the work itself.

### Mode Classification (v6.3.0)

**Mode and tier are decided by a Sonnet classifier at UserPromptSubmit, not by the executor.** `hooks/PromptProcessing.hook.ts` runs on every top-level prompt, calls Sonnet via the same subscription-billed `claude` subprocess pattern Inference.ts uses, and writes a single line into additionalContext:

```
MODE: MINIMAL | NATIVE | ALGORITHM   (always present)
TIER: E1 | E2 | E3 | E4 | E5         (present iff MODE=ALGORITHM)
REASON: <one sentence>
SOURCE: classifier | fail-safe
```

The executor reads this directly. **No regex fallback. No model judgment.** If `MODE` is MINIMAL or NATIVE, the executor uses the corresponding format from CLAUDE.md and stops. If `MODE` is ALGORITHM, the executor enters the Algorithm at the named `TIER`.

**Classifier rules (encoded in the hook's system prompt):**

- **MINIMAL** — greetings, ratings, single-token acknowledgments.
- **NATIVE** — single fact lookup OR single-line edit on a named file OR one command run, AND no new artifact created, AND no multi-step plan.
- **ALGORITHM** — everything else. Includes any build/create/make/implement/design/refactor/migrate/integrate request, anything touching multiple files, anything ambiguous, anything affecting doctrine/system-prompt/hooks/CLAUDE.md/Algorithm/ISA, anything spanning multiple projects, any meta-question about the system itself.
- **Tier (ALGORITHM only)** — E1 trivial (~<90s), E2 single-domain (~3min), E3 multi-file substantial (~10min), E4 cross-cutting/doctrine/architecture (~30min), E5 comprehensive (>2h). Bias higher when in doubt.

**Override hierarchy (executor side):**

1. Explicit `/e1`–`/e5` in the prompt forces tier (and forces ALGORITHM mode if MINIMAL/NATIVE was returned).
2. Otherwise honor classifier output verbatim.
3. **Conversation-context override:** if the classifier returns MINIMAL/NATIVE on a prompt that the conversation context makes clearly ALGORITHM-shaped (e.g., "yes" answering a multi-step proposal, "do it" approving an architecture change), the executor escalates to the appropriate tier and notes the mismatch in `## Decisions`. The classifier sees the prompt in isolation; the executor sees the thread.

**Fail-safe.** Any classifier error path — timeout (25s), non-zero exit, unparseable JSON — defaults to ALGORITHM E3 with `SOURCE: fail-safe` in REASON. Conservative-by-default: under-escalation is the failure mode this system was built to prevent.

**Telemetry.** Every classification is logged to `MEMORY/OBSERVABILITY/mode-classifier.jsonl` with prompt excerpt, mode, tier, reason, source, and latency. Audit weekly: classifier-vs-fail-safe ratio, average latency, downstream override rate.

**Coverage.** The classifier fires on `UserPromptSubmit` — top-level prompts only. Subagent prompts inherit whatever the primary picked. Sonnet latency adds ~3-8s per prompt; this is the deliberate cost of better judgment than regex could provide.

### ISC Quality System

**Every criterion describes one verifiable end-state.** The operational test is granularity:

> **Split until each criterion is one binary tool probe.** A criterion is granular enough when a single tool call (`Read`, `Grep`, `Bash`, `curl`, screenshot, `SELECT`, `bun test`, etc.) returns yes/no on whether it's met. If you cannot name the probe, the criterion is not yet atomic — split it. If the criterion needs human judgment, name the tool-verifiable proxy that stands in for the judgment.

**Tier floor:** the granularity rule produces a natural N. At E2+, that N must meet the tier ISC floor (E2 ≥16, E3 ≥32, E4 ≥128, E5 ≥256). For complex-app project ISAs, the ISC count naturally runs much higher. E1 has no floor — fast-path stays fast.

**Splitting Test** — apply to every criterion as you write it:

| Test | Split when... |
|------|--------------|
| "And"/"With" | Joins two verifiable things |
| Independent failure | Part A can pass while B fails |
| Scope words | "all", "every", "complete" → enumerate |
| Domain boundary | Crosses UI/API/data/logic → one per boundary |
| **No nameable probe** | You can't say which tool would verify it |

**Format:** `- [ ] ISC-N: criterion text` — the criterion phrasing reveals its category. **All ISCs number sequentially as `ISC-N`** — anti-criteria included. ID-stability rule applies: never re-number on edit; splits become `ISC-N.M`.

**Two doctrinal ISC kinds preserved as prose prefix conventions:**

| Kind | Surface form | Rule |
|------|--------------|------|
| **Anti-criterion** — must NOT happen | `- [ ] ISC-N: Anti: <what must NOT happen>` | **≥1 required** |
| **Antecedent** — precondition for target experience | `- [ ] ISC-N: Antecedent: <precondition>` | **≥1 required when goal is experiential** |

**For complex-app projects: the ISA test surface includes (non-exhaustive):**
- **Functional** — features work end-to-end
- **API** — endpoints exist, return expected shape, handle errors
- **Auth** — sign-in/out, token expiry, magic-link flow, session lifecycle
- **Authorization (RBAC/visibility)** — role X can/cannot reach endpoint Y
- **Performance** — latency budgets per route, bundle sizes, query times
- **Security model** — input validation, output encoding, CSRF, rate limits, secret handling
- **Data integrity** — schema invariants, foreign-key consistency, idempotency
- **Build & deploy** — `bun build` succeeds, typecheck clean, deploy version matches
- **Operational** — `/health` returns 200, error budget within SLO, synthetic monitor up

These aren't "in addition to" the ISA — they ARE the ISA. The ISA is the test harness because the ISCs are the tests.

**Allowed status markers:**
- `- [ ]` — pending, not yet verified
- `- [x]` — passed, verified with evidence
- `- [DEFERRED-VERIFY]` — passed in code/intent but live probe is impossible at execution time. **Requires a follow-up task ID in the verification notes.** Cannot be marked `[x]` until the deferred probe runs.

| Deploy | Live URL `curl` or `Interceptor` screenshot showing deployed version |
| UI change | `Skill("Interceptor")` screenshot at the target route |
| Schema/DB change | `SELECT` confirming the migration landed |
| Config/env change | Read-back of the file confirming the new value is on disk |

```

Use `Skill("ISA", "append verification to <isa-path>: ISC-N <probe-type> <evidence>")` to ensure canonical format.

### 🪢 CHECKPOINTS (per-step durability)

Every `[ ]`→`[x]` ISC transition fires `CheckpointPerISC.hook.ts`. For each repo in `~/.claude/checkpoint-repos.txt` with uncommitted changes, the hook auto-commits. Idempotent via sidecar `MEMORY/WORK/{slug}/.checkpoint-state.json`. (v6.2.x: hook will also fire on `<project>/ISA.md` edits once isa-utils discovery lands.)

━━━ ✅ VERIFY ━━━ 6/7

**FIRST ACTION:** Voice `"Entering the Verify phase."`, Edit ISA `phase: verify, updated: {timestamp}`.

### 🛡️ VERIFICATION DOCTRINE

Four rules govern every VERIFY pass.

#### Rule 1 — Live-Probe for User-Facing Artifacts

**If the ISC criterion covers a user-facing artifact, mark it passed ONLY with tool-verified probe evidence.**

| Artifact type | Required probe |
|---------------|----------------|
| Web page / UI | Browser screenshot via `Skill("Interceptor")` |
| HTTP endpoint | `curl` response with expected status + body shape |
| CLI tool output | Actual stdout captured |
| Database write | Subsequent `SELECT` confirming the write |
| File write | `Read` confirming content matches intent |
| Hook / skill | Direct `bun run` invocation with synthetic input |
| Deploy | Verify deployed version string, not just successful push |

**"Should work," "looks fine," "tests pass" are NOT evidence for user-facing criteria.**

**Probe-impossible escape clause:** If a live probe is genuinely impossible at execution time, mark the criterion `[DEFERRED-VERIFY]` with a **required follow-up task ID**.

#### Rule 2 — Commitment-Boundary Advisor Calls

On **multi-step ISAs** (Extended+ effort, multi-file edits, architecture changes), call the advisor at:
1. **Before committing to an approach** — after PLAN, before BUILD begins on the main work
2. **When stuck or diverging** — if the same problem resists two distinct attempts
3. **Once after producing a durable deliverable** — before setting `phase: complete` in LEARN

```bash
bun ~/.claude/PAI/TOOLS/Inference.ts --mode advisor --auto-state \
  "TASK: one-sentence description" \
  "QUESTION: specific decision point or 'any gaps before declaring done?'"
```

#### Rule 2a — Cross-Vendor Audit (Cato, E4/E5 only)

**On Deep (E4) and Comprehensive (E5) ISAs only: after `advisor()` returns and before setting `phase: complete`, spawn Cato for a cross-vendor audit.**

```typescript
Agent({
  subagent_type: "Cato",
  description: "Cross-vendor audit of ISA",
  prompt: `Audit ISA slug ${slug}. Compare artifacts against ISC criteria. Surface Anthropic-family blind spots.`
})
```

| Cato verdict | {{DA_NAME}} action |
|--------------|-----------|
| `pass` with no `critical` findings | Proceed to LEARN |
| `concerns` | Surface findings to user, ask approve / iterate / defer |
| `fail` OR any `critical` finding | Block `phase: complete`, enter Rule 3 |

#### Rule 3 — Conflict-Surfacing

**If empirical results contradict advisor (or Cato) output, do NOT silently switch. Re-call the advisor with the conflict explicitly surfaced.**

**Hard cap on conflict re-calls:** **Maximum TWO re-calls of the advisor on the same conflict.** After the second re-call, escalate to user.

---

**Verify each criterion** — choose the best method at runtime, report evidence:

```
✅ VERIFICATION:
 ISC-N: [method used] — [evidence summary]
 Coverage: N/N passed (N tool-verified, N inspection)
```

- Mark each `[x]` if not already. Use `Skill("ISA", "append verification ...")` for canonical entries.
- **Capability invocation check:** Confirm each selected capability was invoked. Flag any phantom.
- **Thinking floor check (HARD):** Confirm the tier thinking floor was met. Under-floor is a doctrine violation, not a relaxable choice.
- **Delegation floor check (soft):** Under-floor must have a "show your math" justification in `## Decisions`.
- **Tier completeness gate:** Confirm required sections per tier are all populated. Invoke `Skill("ISA", "check completeness")` if uncertain.
- **Doctrine compliance check:** Did Rule 1/2/2a/3 fire as appropriate?
- **Deliverable Compliance check:** Output `📦 DELIVERABLE COMPLIANCE:` checking each D1..DN.

### 🔄 RE-READ CHECK

**Final gate before LEARN. After all other VERIFY checks pass, re-read the user's last message verbatim and enumerate every explicit ask against what actually shipped.**

**Tier gate:** MANDATORY at every tier.

```
🔄 RE-READ:
 🔄 [ask 1 — quote distinctive phrasing]: [✓ addressed | ✗ missed | SKIP reason]
```

**Blocking rule:** ANY `✗` blocks `phase: complete`.

━━━ 📚 LEARN ━━━ 7/7

**FIRST ACTION:** Voice `"Entering the Learn phase."`, Edit ISA `phase: learn, updated: {timestamp}`. Then set `phase: complete`.

```
🧠 LEARNING:
 🧠 [What should I have done differently?]
 🧠 [What would a smarter algorithm have done?]
 🧠 [Did preflight gates fire? Were they useful or wasted effort?]
 🧠 [Did the Verification Doctrine fire? Did it catch anything?]
```

**Changelog entry (NEW v6.2.0):** If structural understanding evolved during this run — a conjecture refuted, a learning crystallized, an ISC added/changed/dropped as a result — append a Changelog entry via `Skill("ISA", "append changelog ...")` in the canonical conjecture/refutation/learning format. The Append workflow refuses to write a partial C/R/L; all four pieces (`conjectured`, `refuted_by`, `learned`, `criterion_now`) are required.

**Reconcile (NEW v6.2.0):** If this run worked against an ephemeral feature file, invoke `Skill("ISA", "reconcile <ephemeral> → <master>")` before setting `phase: complete`. Deterministic merge keyed on stable ISC IDs.

### 🗂️ Learning Router

**Every "should I remember this?" question goes through this single router.**

**Step 1 — Inventory.** For each candidate learning produced this session, classify it:

```
🗂️ LEARNING INVENTORY:
 🗂️ [learning 1 — 8-12 word description] | TYPE: <type> | KEEP: yes/no — <reason>
```

**Default disposition: SKIP.**

**Step 2 — Route + Apply.** For each KEEP=yes learning:

| TYPE | Target surface | Gate |
|------|----------------|------|
| `knowledge` | `MEMORY/KNOWLEDGE/{People\|Companies\|Ideas\|Research}/<slug>.md` | **Inline write.** |
| `rule` | `CLAUDE.md` Operational Rules section | **Inline append.** |
| `gotcha` | The relevant skill's `SKILL.md` Gotchas section | **Inline append.** |
| `state` | `USER/PROJECTS/PROJECTS.md` "Open Sessions to Resume" | **Inline append.** |
| `business` | `USER/BUSINESS/<topic>.md` | **Inline write/append.** |
| `identity` | `USER/PRINCIPAL_IDENTITY.md` / `USER/DA_IDENTITY.md` | **Surface to user.** |
| `doctrine` | Algorithm `PAI/ALGORITHM/v<next>.md` | **Surface to user.** |
| `hook` | New/modified `hooks/*.hook.ts` + `settings.json` registration | **Surface to user.** |
| `permission` | `settings.json` `permissions.deny` / `permissions.allow` | **Surface to user.** |

**Documentation sync** — if this session modified PAI system files, propagate via `Skill("<your-release-skill>", "documentation update — I changed these system files: [comma-separated]")`.

```
📄 DOC SYNC: [N system files changed → invoked DocumentationUpdate | SKIP — no system files modified]
```

## MANDATORY RESPONSE FORMAT — STOP-THE-LINE

**Every Algorithm run MUST close with this exact block. Zero exceptions.**

━━━ 📃 SUMMARY ━━━ 7/7

🔄 ITERATION on: [16 words of context — omit on first response, include on follow-ups]
📃 CONTENT: [Up to 128 lines of the content, if there is any]
🖊️ STORY: [4 8-word bullets in Paul Graham simplicity format for what the problem was, what we did, how it went, and what if anything is next]

**After this block: nothing.**

echo '{"timestamp":"[ISO-8601]","effort_level":"[tier]","effort_source":"[auto|gate-floor|explicit]","task_description":"[TASK line]","criteria_count":[N],"criteria_passed":[N],"criteria_failed":[N],"prd_id":"[slug]","implied_sentiment":[1-10],"satisfaction_prediction":[1-10],"reflection_q1":"[Q1]","reflection_q2":"[Q2]","reflection_q3":"[Q3]","knowledge_flags":[N],"within_budget":[bool],"living_doc_refinements":[N],"doctrine_fired":{"live_probe":[bool],"advisor":[bool],"cato":[bool],"conflict":[bool],"thinking_floor_met":[bool],"completeness_gate_met":[bool]}}' >> ~/.claude/PAI/MEMORY/LEARNING/REFLECTIONS/algorithm-reflections.jsonl
```

- **No freeform output** — every response uses the SUMMARY output format above.

- **Thinking floor (HARD)** — meet the tier thinking floor (E2 ≥2, E3 ≥4, E4 ≥6, E5 ≥8). Cannot be relaxed via show-your-math. - **Tier completeness gate (HARD, NEW v6.2.0)** — required ISA sections per tier are all populated before `phase: complete`. Invoke `Skill("ISA", "check completeness")` to confirm.

content.text:
I've read the ingest layer. The picture is clear, and the answer is more nuanced than "sign up for Basiq" — the engineering seam is clean but the swap is a real project, and there's a hidden cost most people miss. Here's the grounded plan.

━━━ 👁️ OBSERVE → 🧠 THINK → 📋 PLAN (compressed; this is a plan, so it stops here) ━━━

🎯 INTENT: Tell Nick what it actually involves to connect envelope-os straight to Basiq for AU bank feeds instead of going through PocketSmith.

🏹 CAPABILITIES (thinking, E3 floor met): **FirstPrinciples** (what does each provider actually give you) · **IterativeDepth** (PocketSmith vs Basiq, multi-angle) · **ApertureOscillation** (tactical ingest swap vs strategic "why leave PocketSmith") · **ReReadCheck** (final ask-vs-answer gate). Delegation floor — show-my-math: the only investigation was reading 3 ingest files, a directed lookup I did myself per the delegation gate; no agent warranted.

━━━ 📃 SUMMARY ━━━ 7/7

📃 CONTENT:

## The good news: your architecture already isolates the provider

envelope-os keeps everything PocketSmith-specific inside `src/ingest/`. The envelope engine, budget engine, store, and server all consume a neutral `Tx` shape and never touch PocketSmith (the client docstring even says so: *"the envelope engine never talks to PocketSmith"*). So the blast radius of swapping providers is **contained to the ingest layer** — `client.ts`, `map.ts`, the client dependency in `sync.ts`, `backfill.ts`, `secrets.ts`, and the settings handler. Everything downstream is untouched **if you preserve the `Tx` contract**. That seam is the reason this is feasible at all.

## The bad news: PocketSmith and Basiq are not like-for-like

PocketSmith is a finished personal-finance app that has *already* linked the banks and *already* categorised every transaction. You pull aggregated, enriched data with one static key. Basiq is a raw aggregation platform — you have to do the linking, the consent, the polling, and the categorisation yourself. Five concrete differences, each is real work:

1. **Auth & connection lifecycle (much heavier).** Today: one static `X-Developer-Key` header, set once (`client.ts:51`). Basiq: server-to-server token auth (API key → short-lived bearer token you refresh), plus you create a Basiq `user`, plus you host a bank-linking **consent flow** (Basiq Connect / CDR consent UI), then store the resulting `connection`.

2. **Async, job-based fetch.** Today: synchronous `GET` with Link-header pagination, drained by a generator (`paginate()`). Basiq: you POST a connection refresh, get a **job**, poll it to completion, *then* read accounts/transactions. The pull-only `runSync` loop is a rewrite, not a tweak.

3. **CDR consent expiry.** PocketSmith never expires. CDR consents expire (up to 12 months) and must be re-collected — you need a re-consent flow, expiry handling, and the consent-dashboard/withdrawal obligations CDR places on data recipients.

4. **The categorisation gap — this is the biggest hidden cost.** PocketSmith hands you transactions already filed into the user's own category tree, and envelope-os's *entire* envelope assignment is keyed on PocketSmith `category.id` (`map.ts:41` → the envelope engine resolves category→envelope via effective-dated mappings). Basiq gives raw transactions plus its *own* enrichment taxonomy (merchant + Basiq category), which does **not** match your PocketSmith category IDs. So you either rebuild a categorisation layer (Basiq enrich + your own rules engine) or re-key every category→envelope mapping onto Basiq's taxonomy. The envelope engine doesn't change, but its *input contract* does.

5. **Field shapes.** `map.ts` leans on `is_transfer`, `status=="pending"`, signed decimal `amount`, `payee`. Basiq has equivalents but different names/types (direction + string amounts, posted/pending, merchant/description). The mapper is a full rewrite.

## The commercial / accreditation side (the non-engineering part)

- **Development is free and immediate.** Sign up at the Basiq dashboard, get API keys, build against the sandbox/test banks. No accreditation needed to develop.
- **Production CDR data needs onboarding.** Basiq holds the CDR accreditation (you consume it, you don't become an ADR yourself), but production access requires a **paid plan + a commercial onboarding** where they review your use case and you sign agreements. Pricing is per-connection/per-user monthly.
- **Single-user caveat.** Basiq's CDR product is built for businesses serving many consumers. For a personal, single-user app (just your own data) it's arguably heavier and pricier than warranted — **confirm Basiq will onboard a personal/single-user use case, and at what cost, before committing.** (Their non-CDR "direct" connections exist but are being deprecated; don't build new on them.)

## Rough effort (engineering only)

Ingest auth + token + job-poll rewrite ~2-3 days · consent flow + CDR lifecycle ~2-3 days · mapper ~1 day · **categorisation rebuild = the wildcard, days to weeks** depending on approach · plus Basiq commercial onboarding lead time (external, days-to-weeks). Call it a 1-2 week build, dominated by the categorisation decision, fronted by an onboarding wait.

## My read

The seam is clean, so this is doable without disturbing the rest of envelope-os — but it's a genuine project, not a config swap, and the categorisation rebuild is the part that decides the cost. Before scoping further I want to know *why* you're leaving PocketSmith (cost, control, data freshness, dropping a dependency), because the answer changes whether full Basiq CDR is even the right target.

🖊️ STORY:
 • Problem: connect envelope-os straight to Basiq, not via PocketSmith.
 • Did: read ingest layer, mapped the real swap cost.

content.text:
Confirmed the architectural point, and it changes the recommendation. The store is **already multi-tenant** — every method is scoped by `userId`, and `local.ts` literally says *"Local seeds exactly one user over the multi-tenant schema."* Cloud auth already does email magic-link tenant onboarding. So your data model and auth were never the blocker to adding people. PocketSmith was.

━━━ 📃 SUMMARY ━━━ 7/7

🔄 ITERATION on: Nick wants off PocketSmith to drop cost + a bridge dependency, with future multi-user (product) in mind.

📃 CONTENT:

## The reframe your reasoning unlocks

You've found the real structural fact: **envelope-os is already built multi-tenant** — the store is scoped by `userId` on every call, and cloud magic-link onboarding (`auth/cloud.ts`) already mints a tenant per email. The one thing standing between "my budget app" and "a product other people use" was PocketSmith, because it's a *per-user external bridge* — every user would need their own PocketSmith account and subscription. That's not a product, that's a referral.

So moving to Basiq isn't just dropping a cost. It removes the single thing blocking envelope-os from becoming a product. The store and auth are ready; what's missing is the bank-linking + categorisation layer that PocketSmith was silently doing for you. Going to Basiq means **building that bridge yourself, owned and embedded**, so a user just connects their bank inside your app.

## What that resolves

- **Replace, don't run both (#2).** Build a clean `IngestProvider` port (the seam already exists informally), implement Basiq behind it, retire PocketSmith. Keep both only briefly as a personal migration bridge for your own historical data — not as a product feature.
- **You must own categorisation now (#3) — it's no longer a choice.** A product can't require each user to pre-categorise their data (that was PocketSmith's job). So you build a categorisation layer on Basiq's enrichment + your own rules engine. The envelope engine doesn't change; you're rebuilding the *input* that feeds it. This is the largest chunk of the work.

## The new cost that replaces the PocketSmith cost

Serving **other people's** banking data under CDR is a heavier compliance posture than pulling only your own — even though Basiq holds the accreditation. You'd operate as a CDR representative/affiliate under Basiq's model, with consent dashboards, data-minimisation, and deletion obligations. That's the real trade: you swap a per-user subscription cost for a one-time-plus-ongoing compliance surface. For a product, that's the right trade; for just-you, it's overhead.

## My recommendation on sequencing

Build it now **single-user (you), on Basiq, PocketSmith retired** — but architect the ingest/consent/categorisation layer the *product* way (per-user connection objects, hosted consent flow, owned categorisation), so flipping on multi-user later is configuration + compliance onboarding, not a re-architecture. Since the store and auth are already multi-tenant, preserving that path costs almost nothing now and saves a rebuild later. Don't do the multi-user CDR-representative onboarding yet — defer that until you actually open it to others.

Net scope: a contained ingest-layer rewrite (auth/token, job-poll sync, mapper) **plus** a new owned categorisation layer **plus** an embedded Basiq consent flow. Call it ~1.5-2.5 weeks, dominated by categorisation, fronted by Basiq dev-account signup (immediate) — production onboarding deferred until multi-user.

🖊️ STORY:
 • Problem: leave PocketSmith, keep the door open to a product.
 • Did: confirmed store + auth already multi-tenant; PocketSmith was the blocker.
 • Went: clear path — replace via port, own categorisation, build product-shaped.
 • Next: scaffold the ISA + spec the Basiq ingest provider.

3	project: envelope-os

5	effort: deep

13	
14	# Penny (envelope-os) — Project ISA
15	
16	> Surface name **Penny**. Codebase folder `envelope-os`. Zero-based envelope budgeting layer on top of PocketSmith, feeding PAI Pulse. AUD, personal-finance-grade security. **Local-first now, cloud-ready by construction.** One codebase ships to two deployment targets — Local (Tailscale, single principal at runtime) and Cloud (public at `nicholaswood.com.au/budget`, multi-tenant) — and the only difference between them is configuration plus two swapped adapters, never the data model or the business logic.
17	
18	## Problem
19	
20	PocketSmith owns Nick's bank feeds and categorisation across ANZ (primary), NAB (credit card), and Macquarie, but its envelope handling is weak and it does not implement zero-based envelope budgeting. Dave Ramsey's EveryDollar and similar apps do implement the methodology but cannot connect to Australian banks. The result is that Nick runs envelope budgeting in his head on top of PocketSmith, which does not scale, does not survive a credit-card statement cycle cleanly, and gives no trustworthy single number for "where am I against budget right now". There is no time-travel view of envelope balances at a past date, no enforced every-dollar-allocated discipline, and no surface that feeds the state into Pulse. Secondly, the original build was scoped local-only and single-user; if it works, Nick wants the option to let another person use it by handing over only their email and their own PocketSmith developer key, which a local-only, single-tenant design cannot do without a painful retrofit.
21	
22	## Vision
23	
24	Nick opens Pulse and sees one honest line. Unallocated dollars, the worst three overspends, and whether the credit-card holding balance still matches NAB. He opens Penny on his phone — installed as a PWA, reached over Tailscale. He never plans a month; the budget is the recurring template and it simply rolls into each new month on its own. When something changes he adjusts one envelope or moves money, the change is remembered going forward, and it lands in a budget history he can scroll back through. When a late transaction lands weeks later, the envelope it belongs to moves on the day it was spent, not when the statement closes, so the budget never lies about the past. The euphoric surprise is twofold: the holding-versus-NAB tripwire — a single number that, when it drifts, tells Nick something is wrong before he would otherwise have noticed — and the realisation that the day he decides to let someone else use Penny, it is already a per-user multi-tenant app; he adds them with an email and their dev key, flips one config value, deploys to GCP, and nothing in the ledger, the envelope engine, or the UI had to change.
25	
26	## Out of Scope
27	
28	The MVP does not split one category across multiple envelopes. Mapping stays many categories to one envelope. A dedicated sinking-fund target type is not built. Annual envelopes are treated as monthly target divided by twelve for the MVP. There is no mobile quick-add of purchases and no offline transaction capture — the PWA is read-and-allocate over Tailscale, not an offline write queue. There is no auto-allocation engine and no agent-proposed allocations. There is no reporting suite beyond what the grid and detail pages show, no PDF or CSV export, and no what-if replay queries against the event log. There is no multi-currency support. There is no joint-finance surface; the data model is multi-tenant per-user, not joint-account shared-ledger. **Cloud hosting is built-ready, not deployed.** The cloud adapters (email magic-link auth, KMS-encrypted per-user secrets, Postgres data layer) are written and unit-tested behind their interfaces so the switch is config-only, but standing up the public GCP service, registering the `/budget` route on `nicholaswood.com.au`, and onboarding a second human are deliberate later steps, not MVP deliverables. Direct bank-CSV reconciliation against PocketSmith feeds is a later trust layer, not MVP.
29	
30	## Principles
31	
32	- The envelope is the user-facing primitive. PocketSmith categories are inputs. Envelopes are how Nick thinks and decides.
33	- Cash-basis fidelity to the envelope metaphor. A swipe decrements the envelope on the day it happens, regardless of which card moved.
34	- Every dollar is conserved. A forgiven overspend is not free money. The deficit is always booked somewhere, never silently leaked.
35	- Local-first. Personal financial data does not leave the owner's machine without a deliberate, per-action choice. In local mode there is no cloud egress of transactions at all.
36	- **Cloud-ready by construction, not by rewrite.** The data model is multi-tenant from the first migration; every piece of identity-bearing state carries a `user_id`. Deployment differences (who authenticates, where secrets live, which database backs the store) sit behind interfaces. Business logic never knows or branches on which deployment target it is running in.
37	- **One tenant per principal.** Each user owns their own PocketSmith developer key, their own transactions, their own envelopes and budget. There is no shared data between tenants. Onboarding a person is: their email plus their PocketSmith dev key.
38	- The event log is the source of truth and the audit log. Future-Nick can always ask why an envelope went negative on a given day and get an answer.
39	- The thing is the source of truth, not the task. This ISA at the project root is iterated continuously, not recreated per task.
40	
41	## Constraints
42	
43	- bun plus TypeScript only. No Python. No npm or npx. Australian English. AUD only. No em dashes in prose.
44	- **Single codebase, two deployment targets, one switch.** A `DEPLOY_MODE` value of `local` or `cloud` is the only thing that selects deployment behaviour. No business module reads `DEPLOY_MODE`; only the composition root (dependency wiring) does.
45	- **Multi-tenant schema from the first migration.** A `users` table exists. Every tenant-scoped table carries a non-null `user_id` foreign key to `users.id`. Local mode seeds exactly one user (Nick) and runs single-tenant at runtime over a multi-tenant schema. There is no separate single-tenant schema that later needs migrating.
46	- **Auth sits behind an `AuthProvider` interface.** Local implementation: Tailscale device trust plus a PIN held in the secret store, thirty-minute idle session. Cloud implementation: passwordless email magic-link sign-in (request link, verify token, mint httpOnly+Secure+SameSite session cookie). No route handler or business module depends on which implementation is active; they depend only on the resolved authenticated `user_id`.
47	- **Secrets sit behind a `SecretStore` interface, keyed per user.** Each user's PocketSmith `X-Developer-Key` is fetched through the store for the authenticated `user_id` at request time. Local implementation: the PAI secrets store / OS keychain / an encrypted local file. Cloud implementation: envelope encryption via GCP KMS with ciphertext stored in the database. A developer key never appears in env files, git, logs, or as plaintext at rest.
48	- **Data access sits behind a thin store layer; SQL stays Postgres-portable.** Local persistence is SQLite via `bun:sqlite`, single file, single writer owned by one Bun process. No business module imports `bun:sqlite` directly — they depend on the store interface. Business queries avoid SQLite-only syntax so the Postgres adapter (cloud) is a drop-in. The cloud Postgres adapter is written and unit-tested but not the local default.
49	- The PocketSmith client is generated from the published OpenAPI 3 spec `openapi.json` at `github.com/pocketsmith/api`, pinned to commit SHA `8e964ca0107444e4d797b75fbc30fb969d488d9d` in-repo. The client is regenerated manually on a spec bump, never auto-tracked. Base URL `https://api.pocketsmith.com/v2`. Auth is the `X-Developer-Key` header (not OAuth) in local and cloud alike — the key is the per-user secret.
50	- Sync is daily pull only. PocketSmith publishes no webhooks, so no push or listener code path may exist. Incremental sync uses `updated_since`.
51	- **The UI is a PWA, optimised for web app and installed app alike.** It ships a web manifest and a service worker, is installable on iOS and Android home screens, and serves an offline app shell. It is served over HTTPS in both modes: locally via `tailscale serve` on a `*.ts.net` hostname (a real cert, so service workers register and install works); in cloud via the platform certificate at `nicholaswood.com.au/budget`. Remote access in local mode is Tailscale-only; no public internet exposure in local mode.
52	- No cloud SaaS storage of financial data and no cloud AI inference over transactions in local mode. In cloud mode, financial data is stored in the user's own tenant rows and protected per the security ISCs; cloud AI inference over transactions stays off by default and opt-in per query.
53	
54	## Goal
55	
56	Ship a local-first Penny that replaces Nick's PocketSmith-plus-mental-model setup with a real zero-based envelope view, built on a multi-tenant, adapter-seamed architecture that becomes a public per-user cloud app by changing configuration rather than code. Done means: a daily PocketSmith pull lands transactions into a SQLite event-sourced ledger scoped to the authenticated user; envelopes decrement on spend-date with a visible Credit Card Holding envelope for NAB; the recurring budget template auto-rolls into each new month with no manual ritual, a continuous zero-based check alerts when the budget is unbalanced rather than blocking, and actual-versus-budget income variance is carried as surplus/deficit on per-source income envelopes; the grid and a time-travel view render envelope balances; the app runs as an installable PWA reachable over Tailscale HTTPS; a read-only Pulse widget surfaces unallocated dollars, top overspends, and the holding-versus-NAB tripwire; and the cloud-ready seams (multi-tenant schema, `AuthProvider`, `SecretStore`, portable store layer, `DEPLOY_MODE` switch) are in place and unit-tested such that the cloud adapters compile and pass their tests without any business-logic change.
57	
58	## Criteria
59	
60	### Ingest and sync (Weekend 1)
61	
62	- [ ] ISC-1: PocketSmith TypeScript client generated from the pinned OpenAPI 3 commit SHA
63	- [ ] ISC-2: Client authenticates using the X-Developer-Key header
64	- [ ] ISC-3: Developer key resolved through the SecretStore for the authenticated user at runtime
65	- [ ] ISC-4: Backfill pages through the transactions endpoint to completion
66	- [ ] ISC-5: Incremental sync passes updated_since equal to last successful run timestamp
67	- [ ] ISC-6: Backfill script pulls two years from a parameterised start date
68	- [ ] ISC-7: Daily sync runs from PAI cron at a fixed local time
69	- [ ] ISC-8: Two consecutive failed syncs raise a Pulse or Telegram alert
70	- [ ] ISC-9: Anti: No webhook listener or push-sync code path exists anywhere in the repo
71	
72	### Data model and store (Weekend 1 to 2)
73	
74	- [ ] ISC-10: SQLite database opens via bun:sqlite as a single file at a known path
75	- [ ] ISC-11: Schema declares events, snapshots, transactions, categories, mappings, envelopes tables
76	- [ ] ISC-12: Each transaction row stores the raw PocketSmith JSON for diffing
77	- [ ] ISC-13: transaction_overrides table is keyed on pocketsmith id and field
78	- [ ] ISC-14: An owner column exists on ledger entities, defaulted to the single principal
79	- [ ] ISC-15: Every state change appends an event with timestamp, actor, and correlation id
80	- [ ] ISC-16: End-of-day job writes one snapshot balance row per envelope per day
81	- [ ] ISC-17: Anti: Re-sync never mutates a transaction beyond base-field refresh plus overlay
82	
83	### Envelope semantics (Weekend 2)
84	
85	- [ ] ISC-18: Envelope CRUD persists name, parent_id, group, rollover_rule, target_type, target_amount
86	- [ ] ISC-73: Envelopes form a tree via a self-referential parent_id; a parent envelope is itself spendable and allocatable, not just a header
87	- [ ] ISC-74: A parent envelope's carryover, allocation, total, and left roll up as the sum of its children plus any allocation or activity directly on the parent
88	- [ ] ISC-19: Category-to-envelope mapping is many-to-one and effective-dated
89	- [ ] ISC-20: Unmapped category transactions resolve to the Inbox envelope at import
90	- [ ] ISC-21: NAB card spend decrements the Credit Card Holding envelope on transaction date
91	- [ ] ISC-22: Transactions flagged is_transfer are excluded from envelope decrement
92	- [ ] ISC-23: Pending transactions appear in lists but do not decrement balances
